PRELIMINARY ANNOUNCEMENT
TWO INTERNATIONAL DISTANCE SAMPLING WORKSHOPS
_____________________________________________

Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
University of St Andrews
and
Colorado Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Unit

The Research Unit for Wildlife Population assessment announce two 4-day
training workshops in distance sampling, to be held in Fort Collins,
Colorado, USA in June 1999. More information is given below. Please contact
the workshop organizer (address below) to register interest and request
further details.

Workshop Information
--------------------

Title: Design and Analysis of Distance Sampling Surveys

Instructors: Steve Buckland, David Borchers, and Len Thomas
(University of St Andrews)
Bruce Lubow
(Colorado Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Unit)

Dates: Workshop 1: June 14 - 17
Workshop 2: June 21 - 24
(The program for both workshops is the same)

Venue: Fort Collins, Colorado, USA

Cost: TBA

Summary:

Distance sampling is the most widely used method for estimating the abundance
of wildlife populations. The aim of these workshops is to train participants
in both the design and analysis of distance sampling surveys, including line
and point transects. The workshops will be a blend of theory and practice,
and participants will learn the new, windows version of the software
Distance. Participants are encouraged to bring their own data sets. In the
latter part of the workshop, time is set aside for discussion of topics of
common interest in smaller, informal groups.
